rules: Immutable 101 selected artworks; no new human approval inferred.
No new pixels, acquisition, crop rights or production work.
Fra Angelico, El Greco and similar flat stylised proposals excluded; artist-name screening does not replace curator visual judgement.
One canonical artwork object reused across relevant modules, no file duplication.
Exact scene, contextual named saint, Eucharistic allegory and other subjects clearly distinguished.
Bible Atlas P1 83 subjects remain owned by independent research pipeline, no mutations.
Saint icon exception for Our Lady of Perpetual Help requires explicit user decision rather than silent stylistic inconsistency.
Sources establish actual paintings, not universal 1962 feast priority or app permission.

paintings.title: Christ before Pilate
paintings.inventory: Scuola Grande di San Rocco, Sala dell’Albergo, 1566–67
paintings.note: Monumental oil-on-canvas dramatic Christ-before-Pilate. The depicted washing-of-hands incident corresponds to Matthew 27, which is LATER than the dialogue John 18:33–37 appointed on Christ the King under 1962 calendar. Do NOT claim this exact Christ King Gospel; thematic royal-suffering linkage only, no dedicated crowned Christ-king subject. Style aligns with Venetian high Renaissance but image quality unknown.

paintings.title: La visión de san Antonio de Padua
paintings.note: Cathedral's own account authenticates monumental Murillo canvas, Saint Anthony receives the Child Jesus in a dramatic heaven-and-earth Baroque composition. Older option name now anchored to exact custodian record; poor phone hero if crop forces upper/lower split. No rights or user aesthetic approval.

paintings.title: Saint Louis soignant les blessés après la bataille de Mansourah (1250)
paintings.note: French Ministry of Culture museum catalogue confirms 1709 painting commissioned by Louis XIV for altar of Saint Louis in Versailles royal chapel. Named saint and charitable subject, not reliquary Crown of Thorns image or historical portrait.

paintings.title: The Baptism of the King of Cashel by Saint Patrick
paintings.note: National Gallery of Ireland confirms c.1800–1801 oil on paper laid on canvas, 62 × 63 cm, as an UNFINISHED artist oil sketch from a larger original composition. Authentically links Saint Patrick and Cashel baptism but reject automatic masterpiece status until comparison with finished work.

paintings.title: Saint Benedict Destroying Idols
paintings.note: Prado exhibition identifies Fray Juan Andrés Rizi's large pre-1662 oil on canvas, Saint Benedict destroying idols. Separate original object landing page/inventory still to find. NOT equivalent to portraits, and final artist suitability remains open.

paintings.title: The Consecration of Saint Nicholas
paintings.note: National Gallery directly authenticates the 1562 oil-on-canvas original commissioned for San Benedetto Po, 286.5 × 175.3 cm, Vasari-attested master Veronese. Existing 11 October candidate now source-reconciled; no substitute new painting ID.
